title: DITA searchtitle normative behavior
content: Normative DITA behavior for <searchtitle>: a search title is an alternative title intended for display by search tools when the primary topic title is too general in a search-results context. The <searchtitle> convenience element is equivalent to <titlealt title-role="search">, and its processing expectations follow the rules for <titlealt>. This source defines DITA semantics only. It does not define how AEM Guides maps the value to HTML, JCR properties, AEM search indexes, or a specific publishing implementation.
summary: DITA defines searchtitle as an alternative title for search tools and as equivalent to titlealt with title-role search.
learned_behavior: Use searchtitle as alternate search-oriented title metadata; do not infer AEM output mapping from the DITA contract alone.
expected_behavior: searchtitle provides alternate search-oriented title metadata
searchtitle is equivalent to titlealt with title-role search
qa_oracles: Verify source DITA contains searchtitle or titlealt with title-role search
Use product-specific evidence before asserting rendered output
risk_signals: treating DITA semantics as proof of an AEM Sites mapping
confidence_contract: Normative for DITA semantics; not evidence for an AEM Guides output mapping.

title: AEM Guides legacy AEM Sites searchtitle mapping
content: Verified Starling origin/develop implementation for legacy AEM Sites component mapping. elementmapping.xml maps the DITA class '- topic/searchtitle ' to component path fmdita/components/dita/searchtitle, stores the XML in property data, and targets the component to head. The searchtitle.jsp component reads the data property, parses the XML, obtains the element text, and renders <meta name="searchtitle" content="{value}">. Therefore, for this legacy mapping, the grounded verification is to publish with an AEM Sites preset that uses legacy component mapping and inspect the rendered page head for a meta element whose name is searchtitle and whose content equals the source searchtitle text.
summary: Legacy AEM Sites mapping targets searchtitle to the page head and renders meta name searchtitle with the source value.
learned_behavior: For legacy component mapping only, verify searchtitle in the rendered page head as meta name searchtitle.
workflow_cues: publish DITA map with AEM Sites preset
expected_behavior: the component renders meta name searchtitle with the element text
qa_oracles: Publish a topic containing a unique searchtitle value using legacy component mapping
Inspect rendered page source and locate meta name searchtitle in the head
Assert the meta content equals the unique source searchtitle value
risk_signals: using this legacy oracle for composite or newer component mapping
checking HTML title instead of meta name searchtitle
confidence_contract: Verified against Starling origin/develop legacy component files; scope does not extend to composite or newer mappings.

title: AEM Sites searchtitle verification oracles
content: Evidence-backed QA oracle for searchtitle with legacy AEM Sites component mapping. Create a topic whose primary title and searchtitle are deliberately different and whose searchtitle contains a unique marker. Publish the map through the applicable AEM Sites preset. Open the generated Sites page and inspect the rendered HTML source or DOM head. Pass when a meta element has name="searchtitle" and content exactly matching the source searchtitle text. Keep the visible heading, HTML title element, JCR title properties, map-level override behavior, fallback behavior, and AEM search-result ranking as separate checks that require their own implementation or runtime evidence.
summary: Legacy verification checks meta name searchtitle in the rendered page head and exact source-value preservation.
learned_behavior: Use a distinct primary title and unique searchtitle marker; assert only the verified head meta mapping.
expected_behavior: rendered head contains meta name searchtitle
meta content preserves source searchtitle text
qa_oracles: Use a unique marker to avoid false positives
Assert exact meta name and content
Record preset and mapping type with the result
risk_signals: asserting unrelated title or search-index behavior
confidence_contract: Oracle is limited to the rendered legacy meta component and exact value preservation.

title: Searchtitle AEM Sites evidence boundaries
content: Evidence boundary for searchtitle answers. The indexed sources verify DITA searchtitle semantics and the legacy AEM Sites component's meta name="searchtitle" output. They do not verify that searchtitle replaces the HTML <title>, changes the visible H1, populates jcr:title or another JCR property, overrides a topic value from map topicmeta, follows a particular fallback chain when absent, is indexed by a specific AEM search implementation, changes search ranking, or behaves identically with composite or newer component mapping. Do not present any of those claims as expected behavior without a matching product-code path, official product document, or observed runtime result.
summary: Keep title, JCR, precedence, fallback, indexing, ranking, and non-legacy mapping claims unverified until separately evidenced.
learned_behavior: Separate verified legacy meta output from unsupported adjacent searchtitle assumptions.
expected_behavior: unsupported adjacent claims remain explicitly unverified
qa_oracles: Do not reuse the legacy meta oracle as proof of search indexing or title precedence
Require runtime evidence for composite or newer component mapping
confidence_contract: High confidence about what the inspected sources do not establish.
